questions.stem: A batsman has an average of \(32\) runs in his \(45\) innings. The difference between his maximum and minimum score is \(120\). If these \(2\) innings are removed, his average for \(43\) innings comes down to \(30\). What was his minimum score?
questions.keySolution:
Total runs in \(45\) innings = \(45 \times 32 = 1440\)
Total runs in \(43\) innings = \(43 \times 30 = 1290\)
Sum of maximum and minimum scores = \(1440 - 1290 = 150\)
Given: Maximum - Minimum = \(120\)
Solving: Maximum + Minimum = \(150\) and Maximum - Minimum = \(120\)
Adding: \(2 \times Maximum = 270\), so Maximum = \(135\)
Minimum = \(150 - 135 = 15\)

When these two pieces are excluded, the average cost of remaining \(19\) pieces is ₹\(8200\). Find the cost of the cheapest piece.
questions.keySolution:
Total cost of \(21\) pieces = \(21 \times 8500 = 178500\)
Total cost of \(19\) pieces = \(19 \times 8200 = 155800\)
Sum of most expensive and cheapest pieces = \(178500 - 155800 = 22700\)
Given: Most expensive - Cheapest = \(3500\)
Solving: Most expensive + Cheapest = \(22700\) and Most expensive - Cheapest = \(3500\)
Adding: \(2 \times Most expensive = 26200\), so Most expensive = \(13100\)
Subtracting: \(2 \times Cheapest = 19200\), so Cheapest = \(9600\)

questions.stem: A typing test involves \(18\) candidates with an average speed of \(55\) words per minute. The difference between the fastest and slowest typist is \(35\) words per minute. When these two candidates are excluded, the average speed of remaining \(16\) candidates is \(52\) words per minute. What is the speed of the fastest typist?
questions.keySolution:
Total speed of \(18\) candidates = \(18 \times 55 = 990\) wpm
Total speed of \(16\) candidates = \(16 \times 52 = 832\) wpm
Sum of fastest and slowest speeds = \(990 - 832 = 158\) wpm
Given: Fastest - Slowest = \(35\) wpm
Solving: Fastest + Slowest = \(158\) and Fastest - Slowest = \(35\)
Adding: \(2 \times Fastest = 193\), so Fastest = \(96.5\) wpm
Subtracting: \(2 \times Slowest = 123\), so Slowest = \(61.5\) wpm

questions.stem: A coffee shop serves \(29\) beverages with an average preparation time of \(3.5\) minutes each. The difference between the most complex and simplest beverage is \(6\) minutes. After removing these two beverages, the average preparation time for remaining \(27\) beverages is \(3.2\) minutes. Find the preparation time for the simplest beverage.
questions.keySolution:
Total preparation time for \(29\) beverages = \(29 \times 3.5 = 101.5\) minutes
Total preparation time for \(27\) beverages = \(27 \times 3.2 = 86.4\) minutes
Sum of most complex and simplest beverages = \(101.5 - 86.4 = 15.1\) minutes
Given: Most complex - Simplest = \(6\) minutes
Solving: Most complex + Simplest = \(15.1\) and Most complex - Simplest = \(6\)
Adding: \(2 \times Most complex = 21.1\), so Most complex = \(10.55\) minutes
Subtracting: \(2 \times Simplest = 9.1\), so Simplest = \(4.55\) minutes

questions.stem: A language school has \(31\) students with an average test score of \(82\) points. The difference between the highest and lowest score is \(45\) points. When these two scores are excluded, the average score of remaining \(29\) students is \(80\) points. What is the highest score?
questions.keySolution:
Total score of \(31\) students = \(31 \times 82 = 2542\) points
Total score of \(29\) students = \(29 \times 80 = 2320\) points
Sum of highest and lowest scores = \(2542 - 2320 = 222\) points
Given: Highest - Lowest = \(45\) points
Solving: Highest + Lowest = \(222\) and Highest - Lowest = \(45\)
Adding: \(2 \times Highest = 267\), so Highest = \(133.5\) points
Subtracting: \(2 \times Lowest = 177\), so Lowest = \(88.5\) points

questions.stem: A delivery truck makes \(25\) stops with an average time of \(12\) minutes per stop. The difference between the longest and shortest stop is \(22\) minutes. When these two stops are excluded, the average time for remaining \(23\) stops is \(11\) minutes. Find the time for the shortest stop.
questions.keySolution:
Total time for \(25\) stops = \(25 \times 12 = 300\) minutes
Total time for \(23\) stops = \(23 \times 11 = 253\) minutes
Sum of longest and shortest stops = \(300 - 253 = 47\) minutes
Given: Longest - Shortest = \(22\) minutes
Solving: Longest + Shortest = \(47\) and Longest - Shortest = \(22\)
Adding: \(2 \times Longest = 69\), so Longest = \(34.5\) minutes
Subtracting: \(2 \times Shortest = 25\), so Shortest = \(12.5\) minutes

questions.stem: A research team conducts \(20\) surveys with an average response time of \(15\) minutes each. The difference between the longest and shortest survey is \(18\) minutes. When these two surveys are excluded, the average response time for remaining \(18\) surveys is \(14\) minutes. What is the response time for the longest survey?
questions.keySolution:
Total response time for \(20\) surveys = \(20 \times 15 = 300\) minutes
Total response time for \(18\) surveys = \(18 \times 14 = 252\) minutes
Sum of longest and shortest surveys = \(300 - 252 = 48\) minutes
Given: Longest - Shortest = \(18\) minutes
Solving: Longest + Shortest = \(48\) and Longest - Shortest = \(18\)
Adding: \(2 \times Longest = 66\), so Longest = \(33\) minutes
Subtracting: \(2 \times Shortest = 30\), so Shortest = \(15\) minutes
